title: A Portrait for the Well
premise: Silas Thornbury, a folklorist who has spent years keeping herself unremarkable and unremembered, arrives in the drowned-farm village of Hollowmere to record songs no one will sing twice. When the church bell—melted down in 1911—begins ringing at night, she learns the village's founders bound something beneath the old well with a ritual left deliberately unfinished, and that her own forgotten childhood is stitched into it. As the well refills and villagers begin remembering her against her will, Silas must choose between remaining invisible and claiming an identity she buried, finishing the founders' ritual by giving the well a true name before the water rises on the solstice. In the end she completes the rite at terrible cost, trading her anonymity for belonging, and Hollowmere's survivors carry her song forward—the one song they now sing twice.
about_author: Petra Vasquez is a former archivist of regional folk music who spent a decade collecting ballads in remote farming communities before turning to horror. She writes in a converted chapel, keeps the doors counted, and insists every story she tells was sung to her first.

chapters.title: The Census of Doors
chapters.summary: Silas arrives in Hollowmere, counting doorways out of habit and renting a room from the brusque innkeeper Maren Cole. POV: Silas. The beat is wary calm—a woman whose whole life is the discipline of being overlooked, settling into a place that seems to overlook her already.

chapters.title: Songs They Won't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: At the tavern, Silas records a harvest round; the singer stops mid-verse, pale, refusing to repeat a single line. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into unease as she realizes the refusal is universal, practiced, almost liturgical.

chapters.title: What the Bell Was Made Into
chapters.summary: In the church archive, Silas finds records: the bell was melted in 1911, recast as a well-cover plate. The vicar, Edwin Marsh, watches her too closely. POV: Silas. Beat: the first crack in the village's story, and the sense of being observed rather than ignored.

chapters.title: Ringing
chapters.summary: Past midnight, a bell tolls eleven times though there is no bell. Silas finds the whole village awake, standing in doorways, counting along. POV: Silas. Beat: dread and a strange kinship—these are people who count things too.

chapters.title: Maren's Version
chapters.summary: Maren admits the ringing has happened before, always before a drowning. She warns Silas to leave, then asks her to stay—one contradiction too many. POV: Silas with a brief Maren interlude. Beat: the first offer of trust, refused and wanted at once.

chapters.title: The Plate Over the Water
chapters.summary: Silas visits the capped well; the melted bell-plate is scored with names, one of them half-legible: Thornbury. She has no family, no history she trusts. POV: Silas. Beat: identity as wound—the past she fled may have been waiting here.

chapters.title: A Child Who Wasn't Kept
chapters.summary: Old Tam Yew recalls a girl sent away after the last filling, sixty years ago; his memory of her face is Silas's face. POV: Tam, then Silas. Beat: vertigo of recognition—she was here, and someone chose to make her forgettable.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: In the vestry, Silas and Edwin find the founders' ledger: a ritual begun in 1811, pages torn out, instructions ending mid-sentence at 'and give it the name of—'. POV: Silas. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose; the ritual is unfinished and the well is rising.

chapters.title: Remembering Her
chapters.summary: Villagers begin greeting Silas by name, unprompted, their eyes wet—as if remembering her is painful and compulsory. The more they remember, the louder the bell. POV: multiple villagers, then Silas. Beat: invisibility failing; found family arriving like a flood.

chapters.title: The Drowned Lane
chapters.summary: Following ledger references, Silas wades the flooded lane beneath the reservoir and finds the original wellhead, older than the village, breathing cold air upward. POV: Silas. Beat: awe and terror entwined; the geography itself is a throat.

chapters.title: What Sings Back
chapters.summary: At the wellhead, Silas hums the forbidden verse; something below hums it back a half-beat behind, learning her voice. POV: Silas. Beat: intimate horror—the thing isn't monstrous so much as lonely, and it knows her songs.

chapters.title: Edwin's Confession
chapters.summary: Edwin admits the vicars have kept the ritual broken on purpose: a finished rite requires a named sacrifice from the founding line. He hoped Silas would never come back. POV: Edwin. Beat: betrayal braided with protection; the village's kindness has always had a price tag.

chapters.title: The Half-Name
chapters.summary: Silas deciphers that the founders bound the well with a false name, and only its true name—held by the sent-away child—can seal or free it. Her erased identity is the missing page. POV: Silas. Beat: the theme crystallizes: memory is the lock and the key.

chapters.title: Doors Opening
chapters.summary: The solstice nears; water rises through floors, and every door in the village stands open at dawn whether locked or not. Maren counts them and comes up one extra. POV: Maren. Beat: siege atmosphere; the village's order dissolving into the thing it repressed.

chapters.title: Tam's Lullaby
chapters.summary: Dying Tam sings Silas the lullaby she was taken away with—the song containing her true name, worn smooth by his guilt. POV: Tam. Beat: grief and grace; found family delivering the inheritance blood would not.

chapters.title: They Sing It Twice
chapters.summary: Silas teaches the lullaby to Maren, Edwin, and the others, breaking the taboo: sung twice, the name holds. The bell rings continuously now. POV: Silas. Beat: defiance becoming communion; the village choosing her over its own silence.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: On solstice eve, Silas goes down through the wellhead with the ledger, the lullaby, and a lamp, while the village holds the doors shut above. POV: Silas. Beat: sacrificial resolve; the loner walking toward connection by walking under.

chapters.title: The Refilling
chapters.summary: Below, Silas meets what the founders drowned—not a devil but the village's discarded dead and unwanted memories, wearing her childhood face among them. POV: Silas. Beat: horror turning to pity; the monster is everything they refused to remember.

chapters.title: Give It the Name
chapters.summary: Climax: Silas speaks her true name into the rising water, completing the founders' sentence, offering herself as the named sacrifice—but the villagers, singing above, give the name back to her, making it hers instead of the well's. POV: Silas. Beat: terror transfigured into belonging; identity given, not taken.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: The well drains to a quiet spring; the bell falls silent mid-toll. Silas surfaces alive, changed—visible, known, unable to fade anymore. POV: Silas. Beat: exhausted relief and the cost made plain: she can never be invisible again.

chapters.title: The Naming of Things
chapters.summary: The village buries the ledger, repairs the church, and quietly makes room for Silas—a room with her name on the door. Maren counts doors and gets the right number. POV: Maren. Beat: tender aftermath; found family formalized in small domestic rituals.

chapters.title: Coda: Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Months later, Silas records the harvest round complete, and the whole village sings it twice, once for the living and once for the well. The final verse carries her name. POV: Silas. Beat: resolution—memory kept willingly, identity sung rather than hidden.
